goal: Rebase Kimi Code Agent on the OpenCode execution runtime while retaining Kimi as the default provider, the existing macOS distribution channel, local-first storage, Worktree isolation, and human-reviewed merges.
description: The product must replace the current fragmented execution paths with one OpenCode-derived local session, tool, permission, plugin and MCP runtime. It needs predictable Supervisor DAG orchestration, independent worker context, durable task recovery, public-read web research without repeated prompts, native macOS adapters for Browser and Computer Use, complete audit trails, and a polished desktop interaction model. Parallel read-only work is allowed, while Worktree writes, Browser, Computer Use, and destructive actions remain serialized and permission-gated.
tasks: Admit durable user inputs and run provider turns through an OpenCode-derived session engine
Route Kimi API, Kimi Code, and compatible providers through one typed provider boundary
Execute file, shell, web, MCP, browser, and computer-use tools through one permission and receipt protocol
Coordinate Explore, Plan, Implement, Test, Review, Debug, Browser, and Research workers with a dependency graph
Create isolated Worktrees for independent implementation work and inherit them for validation and debugging
Persist session history, tool intents, receipts, artifacts, usage, and recovery checkpoints locally
Expose structured activity, approvals, diffs, terminal output, browser artifacts, and final answers in the desktop UI
Manage Skills, Hooks, MCP servers, and Plugins with capability discovery, isolation, health checks, and recovery
Enforce local security boundaries for filesystem, shell, network, credentials, and destructive Git actions
Measure per-stage token usage, latency, quality, retries, and cost budgets
safety_requirements: Validate tool schema and resource boundaries before permission prompts
Persist intent before any side effect and receipt after settlement
Never replay a successful receipt or automatically replay unknown writes
Reject writes outside the active Worktree
Allow public read-only web research by task or domain while blocking private targets
Keep secrets in Keychain or an encrypted local vault and redact logs
Require explicit approval for shell, destructive Git, Browser writes, and Computer Use
Maintain auditable event history and explicit user-driven recovery
integration_requirements: OpenCode session, provider, tool, MCP, skill, hook, plugin and server semantics
Kimi API and Kimi Code authentication and model selection
Existing Swift Browser Verification and Computer Use adapters
Git Worktree, Diff Review, Terminal PTY, GitHub and GitLab workflows
Kimi SwiftUI/AppKit shell as the only production UI; OpenCode runs headlessly on loopback only
DMG and ZIP GitHub Release distribution with signatures and checksums
